d4m3-a1.title: Section Audit — the Mediation Binder as drafted
d4m3-a1.kicker: Audit all six sections before Atty. Thorne approves delivery.
d4m3-a1.intro: Atty. Grant Mercer says Keystone will not put a real number on the table while the medical ledger is unverified, and on this draft he is right: it was built from the providers' original bills. Two landmines are in the numbers; the rest are in what the set carries and what it leaves out.

items.as: Parties, counsel and mediator only; no start time, location or video link, and no fee split.
items.issue: On the morning of 03/18/2027 nobody can tell from the binder where to be, when, or who pays the mediator. Atty. Mercer's contact was copied from the answer of 11/12/2026 and has not been verified since.
items.fix: Take the start time, location and the carrier's video link from the mediator's confirmation and the fee split from the mediation order; verify every contact and date it.

items.as: Nine pages, unmarked, with three copies tabbed for the mediator, defense counsel and the carrier.
items.issue: A confidential statement is for the mediator alone. Three tabbed copies hand our position, our concessions and our read of the gap straight to Atty. Mercer and to Keystone, and it cannot be undone.
items.fix: Mark every page for the mediator only, cut it to one copy, route it to Atty. Thorne for approval, and calendar its delivery with the binder.

items.as: Four pages of Atty. Thorne's internal summary, filed behind the statement "for context".
items.issue: It sets out our own gap risk, our own valuation and our internal dates. In a binder that three other people will hold, it is the single most damaging page in the set.
items.fix: Pull it to the attorney's set and tell Atty. Thorne it was in the draft. It never goes in a Demand Package, a Mediation Binder or an exhibit set.

items.as: The pre-filing draft: unsigned, no case number, Property Damage not pleaded.
items.issue: A superseded draft is not the operative pleading. It also omits the Property Damage count, so the binder understates what is actually in suit and invites an argument about what was pleaded at all.
items.fix: Replace it with the Complaint filed 09/24/2026, No. 26-CV-04417, and take the draft out of the binder set entirely.

items.as: Not in the set. The pleaded allegations sit in the answer with nothing opposite them.
items.issue: Every allegation in the answer of 11/12/2026 is already answerable from documents on this file. Without the map the mediator hears each one answered by a sentence instead of a page, and Atty. Thorne has to find the exhibit himself.
items.fix: Add the map: each pleaded allegation against the exhibit that answers it, by exhibit number. Flag the two legal questions for Atty. Thorne rather than answering them.

items.as: Four stills, grayscale export of the 02/19/2026 working copy.
items.issue: The same grayscale export that failed QC in the Demand Package. It is the exhibit that answers "the Escape entered out of turn", and in grayscale the stop line is hard to read.
items.fix: Re-export the stills in color from the native file, hash unchanged, and enclose the preservation and chain-of-custody log.

items.what: Riverton Fire EMS Run Report and the event data recorder
items.as: Certified Run Report, and the vendor's download with its chain of custody attached.
items.issue: Together they answer the unbelted defense with data rather than testimony: "restrained front-seat passenger" on the date of loss, and the belt buckled at 11 mph.
items.fix: Confirm each chain of custody travels with its record, and that both are paired against the unbelted allegation in the defense map.

items.what: Keystone's acceptance of Property Damage liability and the deposition summary
items.as: Neither is in the set.
items.issue: Keystone accepted Property Damage liability in writing on 02/17/2026, and John Doe was deposed on 02/18/2027 with the certified transcript already on the file. The binder goes into the room without either.
items.fix: Add the 02/17/2026 letter behind §4, and a deposition summary with the transcript pages on the gap, the April break, the 2021 visits and the seatbelt. Its weight is Atty. Thorne's call.

items.as: Typed from the bills in the file: Riverton Spine & Rehab $6,290.00, total $16,586.40.
items.issue: The Demand Package served 07/20/2026 put the same damages at $16,401.40. Two numbers for one file is exactly the unverified ledger Atty. Mercer named, and the difference is the 05/04/2026 duplicate.
items.fix: Rebuild the ledger line by line from the certified bills in hand: 33 visits × $185.00 = $6,105.00, medical $14,817.40 plus wages $1,584.00 = $16,401.40.

items.as: Shown as a $3,400.00 open balance, and again as a $3,400.00 lien in the lien summary.
items.issue: Peach State paid Crescent $1,860.00 at the contract rate and the provider cannot bill the member the adjustment. Carried into the binder it concedes $3,400.00 that nobody is owed, straight out of John Doe's net.
items.fix: Show the charge satisfied by the plan's contract payment, proved by Peach State's EOB and the corrected $0.00 statement; open liens are Peach State $1,860.00 plus Riverton Spine & Rehab $6,105.00 = $7,965.00.

items.what: Riverton Spine & Rehab's Final Itemized Ledger
items.as: Requested 02/08/2027, chased 02/22, red-flagged 03/01; still outstanding, and the line is not marked.
items.issue: An unqualified figure for a record we do not yet hold is how a ledger becomes unverifiable. The chase is the Case Manager's; whether to go further than a second request is not.
items.fix: Mark the line "Pending Final Verification", keep chasing the certified ledger, and put the subpoena question to Atty. Thorne with the request history.

items.as: Loss of Use and Diminished Value folded into the same damages ledger.
items.issue: Property Damage sits outside the $40,000 stack and is contested separately. Mixed into the bodily injury ledger it inflates the Specials and lets the carrier attack the whole ledger through the Diminished Value dispute.
items.fix: Set Property Damage out in its own schedule: Loss of Use 48 days × $42.00 = $2,016.00; Diminished Value $3,600.00 on the appraisal against Keystone's $792.00.

items.as: Signed original of 06/30/2026, with the 02/09–02/13/2026 call-out record attached.
items.issue: It proves the $1,584.00 wage claim and, separately, that John Doe was calling out of work with neck pain before he ever saw a provider.
items.fix: Confirm the call-out record stays attached to it, so the wage proof and the gap corroboration are read together.

items.as: The adjuster's own letter with her stated reasons for $3,500.
items.issue: The carrier's reasons in its own words are what the mediator needs to see, and they are the reasons the record already answers.
items.fix: Confirm it sits with the Negotiation Log so the offer and its answer are read together.

items.what: Negotiation Log, draft release and the UM consent requests
items.as: None of the three is in the set.
items.issue: Nobody in the room is sure of Keystone's last number, and if the file settles on the day there is no release to sign and no consent on the way to the UM carriers, so the money stops anyway.
items.fix: Add the Negotiation Log from the 07/20/2026 demand to the suit filed 09/24/2026, the draft Limited Release of Robert Smith and Keystone only, and both drafted consent requests.

items.as: Diaried 03/31/2027, the date read off the Scheduling Order.
items.issue: 03/31/2027 is the court's deadline for the mediation to be completed, not the session date. The session is 03/18/2027 and the mediator's confirmation requires the statement and binder seven days before, so 03/31 is twenty days too late.
items.fix: Docket delivery for 03/11/2027 with the approval step ahead of it, and keep 03/31/2027 on the calendar as the court's completion deadline.

items.as: No exhibit numbers, no Bates ranges; the printed binder is the only copy of the order.
items.issue: Without numbers and ranges nobody can be sent to a page, and a printed binder that is the only index cannot be corrected once three people hold copies.
items.fix: Build the index in the CMS exhibit index, where it governs: every document in exactly one section with its number and Bates range, the PDF OCR-searchable and bookmarked.

d4m3-a1.revealNote: The Mediation Binder as Atty. Thorne approved it on 03/10/2027 and the firm delivered it on 03/11/2027: six sections, 141 pages, with the defense map and the rebuilt ledger. The arbitration exhibits and Day 5 both start from it.
revealPoints: Specials rebuilt to $16,401.40, the same figure the Demand Package served on 07/20/2026.
Open liens $7,965.00: Peach State $1,860.00 and Riverton Spine & Rehab $6,105.00; Crescent $0.00.
Riverton Spine & Rehab marked "Pending Final Verification" until its certified ledger arrives.
All five pleaded allegations mapped to answering exhibits; two legal questions flagged, not answered.
Section 2 marked for the mediator only, one copy; the Master Case Summary withdrawn to the attorney's set.
Delivered 03/11/2027, seven days before the 03/18/2027 session; 03/31/2027 kept as the court's deadline.

d4m3-a2.title: Sorting & QC Audit — the arbitration exhibit folder
d4m3-a2.kicker: Sort into six tabs and apply each tab's QC rule as the record lands.
d4m3-a2.intro: Harbor Point and Cardinal State are on the other side of this hearing now, and the folder still holds everything the litigation sub-file collected. Decide for each record which tab it belongs in, or that it is withheld — and apply the QC as you sort, not after.

columns.as: As it came out of the sub-file

items.what: BI tender, Limited Release and the dismissal of Robert Smith
items.as: Keystone's 08/12/2026 tender, the release signed 03/18/2027, and the term sheet.
items.issue: UM opens only once the bodily injury layer is exhausted. These are the threshold exhibits, and they lead the set: nothing about damages matters until exhaustion is proved.
items.fix: Place them at Tab 1 as the first exhibits, C-1 onward, with both Coverage Letters; hold the term sheet itself for Atty. Thorne's decision as a settlement document.

items.as: In the pile, still marked for the mediator only.
items.issue: It was delivered to the mediator alone, and the carriers it was written about are now the opposing parties. Exchanging it hands Harbor Point and Cardinal State our position and our concessions in our own words.
items.fix: Withhold it from the exchange set and record why. A document marked for the mediator does not travel to the next forum.

items.as: Unsigned, no case number, Property Damage not pleaded.
items.issue: A superseded draft offered as a pleading is an invitation to argue about what was actually pleaded, in a forum where the tort case is no longer the claim at all.
items.fix: Take it out of the set. The filed pleadings go to the attorney's set for Atty. Thorne's decision on whether the tort pleadings are exchanged here.

items.as: Public redacted portal copy: witness and party identifiers blacked out.
items.issue: The redactions remove the independent witness and the citation — the two things the report is in the set to prove. Offered this way it proves almost nothing.
items.fix: Order the certified complete report, redact only what this forum requires, and flag the citation's admissibility to Atty. Thorne rather than arguing it.

items.as: Grayscale export, with the preservation log.
items.issue: Third forum, same grayscale export. The carriers dispute damages, not liability, but the mechanism is what makes the injury credible, and an illegible still does not show it.
items.fix: Re-export in color from the native file, hash unchanged, and log the chain of custody with the exhibit.

items.as: Vendor report with chain of custody attached.
items.issue: Belt buckled, 11 mph: objective data on the mechanism, with a foundation already logged. It belongs in the liability tab as it stands.
items.fix: Log its authentication in the exhibit index with the rest of Tab 3, and keep the vendor's chain of custody with it.

items.what: Provider bills and records, six providers
items.as: As received from portals and mailings; no certification from any provider, and none requested.
items.issue: An uncertified record is a record a carrier can object to, and the whole $14,817.40 ledger rests on them. Thirty-six days before the exchange, nothing has been asked for.
items.fix: Request a certification from every provider and from Riverton Fire, Riverton PD and Northgate HR, and log each receipt. Nothing back in 14 days means a second request and a subpoena flag for Atty. Thorne.

items.as: Signed original of 06/19/2026, silent on the 2021 low-back visits.
items.issue: Defense counsel pressed the prior-injury line at the 02/18/2027 deposition, and these carriers are citing the gap. The letter answers the gap and the degenerative reading, but says nothing about 2021.
items.fix: Pair it with the 2021 records, the providers' own histories and the deposition testimony, and flag to Atty. Thorne whether to seek a supplemental declaration from Dr. Reyes. That is his decision, not the Case Manager's.

items.what: LSH intake questionnaire in the client's hand
items.as: The firm's own intake form, completed 02/09/2026.
items.issue: It is a source the firm works from, not evidence, and it carries the client's own rough first account — including the prior-history note our file had to correct. Exchanged, it becomes an impeachment exhibit against him.
items.fix: Withhold it. The records it pointed us to are the exhibits; the questionnaire itself stays in the file.

items.as: Certified by the reporter, 02/18/2027.
items.issue: Certified sworn testimony that he had no prior neck complaint: the human half of the prior medical shield, alongside the 2021 records.
items.fix: Place it at Tab 5 with the pages on the gap, the April break, the 2021 visits and the seatbelt marked in the index.

items.as: Signed original of 06/30/2026.
items.issue: Nine shifts × 8 hours × $22.00 = $1,584.00, proved by the employer. Tab 6 takes wage proof and nothing else.
items.fix: Place it alone at Tab 6, with the 02/09–02/13/2026 call-out record attached to it.

items.what: Impasse memorandum and the Negotiation Log
items.as: Internal memorandum of 09/08/2026 setting out our own strategy, with the log of every offer.
items.issue: Work product and a record of settlement communications. A trainee who files it because it explains the history has put our strategy, and every number we discussed, in front of the carriers.
items.fix: Hold both in the attorney's set and put the privilege and exchange question to Atty. Thorne. Nothing is exchanged, and nothing is withheld, on the Case Manager's own decision.

items.as: Listed on the attorney's-set Lien Sheet because MedPay paid $5,000.00 of the bills.
items.issue: Harbor Point gave up any reimbursement right in writing on 03/02/2026, and it is the carrier on the other side of this hearing. Working John Doe's net from a lien it does not hold costs him $5,000.00 it would never have asked for.
items.fix: Strike it, citing the 03/02/2026 letter in the threshold record. MedPay paying a bill does not create a lien.

items.as: Listed at its invoice amount.
items.issue: MedPay paid Summit's invoice in full on 03/25/2026. The provider has no claim left to assert, so the line is $2,395.00 of John Doe's recovery given away to nobody.
items.fix: Strike it against the MedPay payment ledger. A bill that appears in the Specials is not a lien unless someone is still owed it.

items.as: Listed from the itemized ledger as received, 34 lines.
items.issue: The same 05/04/2026 duplicate, now inside the figure the attorney would negotiate the client's net from. Audited liens are $1,860.00 plus $6,105.00 = $7,965.00, not the $15,545.00 the sheet shows.
items.fix: Correct it to $6,105.00 against the Final Itemized Ledger and the attendance log, and reconcile the sheet to $7,965.00 before it goes to Atty. Thorne.

items.as: Diaried 06/12/2027, ten days before the hearing.
items.issue: Ten days before the hearing lands on a Saturday. A brief diaried for a day the forum is not open is a brief filed late, in the one filing that frames the whole hearing.
items.fix: Count backward and docket the earlier business day, 06/11/2027, as configured for this training file; confirm the forum's rules with Atty. Thorne. Hold the Tab 1 slot for the final brief, never a draft.

items.what: Exhibit numbering and the authentication log
items.as: The folder is unsorted and unnumbered: no C-numbers, no Bates ranges, no authentication column.
items.issue: At the hearing an exhibit nobody can cite is an exhibit nobody uses, and a record with no logged foundation is one the carriers can object to before it is read.
items.fix: Number C-1 onward in the order the tabs run, give each exhibit its Bates range matching its page count, and complete the authentication column before the 06/02/2027 exchange.

d4m3-a2.revealNote: The Arbitration Binder as Atty. Thorne approved it on 05/29/2027 and the firm exchanged it on 06/02/2027: six tabs, exhibits C-1 to C-18, 174 pages, with the withheld-items list and the audited Lien Sheet.
revealPoints: Threshold exhibits lead: the BI tender, both UM consents, the Limited Release and the dismissal.
Every record certified and authenticated; Crescent's certification chased with a subpoena flag.
Tab 5 pairs the 2021 low-back records and the deposition testimony with the MRI read and the Causation Letter.
Lien Sheet audited from $15,545.00 to $7,965.00: MedPay, Summit and Crescent all at $0.00.
Six items withheld on Atty. Thorne's recorded decision, each with its reason on the file.
